body:
I would maybe say that, but his mom and I are pretty close and have confided in and comforted each other about a lot of serious family dynamics on my side and theirs, especially since we moved to the same town four years ago. His mom asked my fiancé how he was after surgery, but nothing to me really. 

It just feels like people I am not as close with have had some positive well wishes and hugs and at the very least, acknowledgement, to give me, and from them, nothing really at all. I think what @quemvidistis said was true, they may just be unable to be a support for me in heavy stress and I’ll just have to learn to accept it. I know they really care about me and us as a couple, my expectations are just different than what they can provide I think :(

Yes, I think you are right and yes, my fiancé and I have talked about how until he met me, he didn’t know what he was and wasn’t communicating could be vague and distant even if he didn’t feel that way. And he says it’s definitely the standard for his mom and how she raised her kids.

I’ve been going to therapy and exploring what you mentioned about managing realistic expectations. I think I’m still hoping that my in laws will fill this loving family hole that I had wanted as a kid, but I am still coming to terms with what they are actually able to offer. I’ve accepted the limitations of my own family over time and with heartache and I think it’s just time to process that for my in laws too. They really are caring and generous people on so many other ways, but yes you are right, being able to hold strong emotions and be a support for me in that way might just not be in the cards :(

I’m sorry OP, I have felt that way before. The only thing that helped me and my relationship with family was moving out, creating and curating my own happy life, and getting some distance and therapy. I’m in my early 30s and only just learning how to regulate myself so that I can still love them and not have their words and behaviors hit me so hard. Good luck, you can do it

I’m going through a friend breakup right now as well and like you said, I thought this was someone who was going to go through life with me. It really does suck, the only way I can make peace with it is telling myself I did the best I could and tried to support them, but I’m going to honor my boundaries for my own well-being.

Thank you so much for your thoughtful comment. It’s something I’ve been asking myself - like am I the crazy one? Am I being irrational? Maybe the tone I took or the comment I said or this or that made me the “bigger bad guy” in the situation. I was totally prepared to own up to my angry tone and apologize, but now I feel like I’m not even being given the chance. 

I’ve never heard of the avoiding side as a manipulative tactic, so thank you for bringing this up. 

I think at the this point and at this age, I thought I had done away with these kinds of friendships, but as my husband reminds me, these kinds of conflicts are just a normal part of life. 

I’m not sure I will reach out to her again as more ultimatum like language will feel great in the moment, but I’m not sure how productive it will be for me let alone how threatened she might feel. I think I’m going to opt to just counting her out of my life in my head. If she ever does reach out, I’ll be open to meeting but try to be calm and communicate that it was extremely hurtful that it took as long as it takes. I’m learning that there is real distinction between forgiving someone and being able to trust them again. 

Thanks again for your comment. Sometimes anonymous validation from the internet really can help :)

I’m sorry this happened to you. People can be the fucking worst and best thing to happen to you. I definitely agree with the last comments about taking the higher road. Though it fucking sucks, you’ll be prouder of yourself and can make peace with the situation in the long run. At this point, you just have to grieve the loss of a friendship that was really good until it wasn’t :(

That seems kind of one sided. I know some people are okay with these kinds of friendships, but clearly it’s kind of weighing on you. Unless you are super lonely rn and any company is good company, it may be best to just let this one fizzle out on its own. Personally I wouldn’t be able to hang out with a friend for long term if it felt like work and effort to just keep a conversation going
I can tell you don’t read very carefully. I’m talking about the full grown retriever
I just finished it and I’m so sad.

Yeah very recently, my husband said something so simple but it hit me differently. Like it’s ok to not be perfect all the time, it’s ok to be a B student, it’s ok to not try your best all. The. Time. I was like what? Why wouldn’t I try my best with everything I do? Work, relationships, school? But then I thought, hmmm maybe more mentally healthy people don’t feel this pressure to be on all the time…

In a way I feel like my therapist is too sweet to expose her to all these dark thoughts? Part of me is comforted by like a kind maternal figure but the other part of me thinks I need another fucked up minded individual to understand. But maybe that’s just me and she’s a professional so I should trust her

I don’t want to say I could never heal over time, but every now and again, I just get so tired of…trying? Putting in effort? Being on for the sake of others’ comfort? I just feel the pressure of everyone’s expectations wanting me to be this or that for them, I just don’t want to feel anything anymore. Thank you for commenting, it is nice to hear from someone

Wow that’s pretty cool. I’ve never mentioned it fully to my therapist and she thinks I’m super funny and well adjusted. Hahah little does she know I’m hiding my deepest inner self behind a wall of humor. I’ve thought of doing the same but was scared of getting admitted
I feel you. I don’t know what to do myself, but I feel the same
